title: The Alien Naturalist
prompt: Describe a mushroom as though you have never seen one before. Avoid the words mushroom, cap, stem, and gills.
group: Take turns describing the same find. A partner tries to locate the features you described without naming the species.
discussion: Which description helped you notice something you had missed?
insight: Careful observation starts before we reach for familiar labels.

title: The Beautifully Wrong Hypothesis
prompt: Invent a possible explanation for a mushroom’s shape. What observation could show that your explanation is wrong?
group: Share two competing explanations. Ask another person what evidence would help distinguish them.
discussion: What finding would make you change your mind?
insight: A scientific explanation becomes useful when we can test it.

title: The Color Thief
prompt: Look closely at a mushroom and find three colors a photograph might miss. What could change the way those colors appear?
group: Compare your descriptions and photos of the same visible surface. Notice the light and camera differences without moving the fungus.
discussion: When would you trust a color comparison?
insight: Light, cameras, and perception all affect how we record color.
resourceLabel: Read the field guide to light and colour

title: Twenty Questions, Zero Answers
prompt: Find a fungus and write five questions about it without answering any of them. Which question would you investigate first?
group: Pool the questions. Choose one the group could investigate on a future walk.
discussion: What evidence could help you answer it?
insight: Better questions often lead to better investigations.
resourceLabel: Explore the ways mycologists investigate fungi

title: The One-Square-Meter Universe
prompt: Choose one small patch of ground. How many different signs of fungal life or decomposition can you notice?
group: Look at the same patch from different safe viewpoints. Compare what each person noticed. Leave the ground undisturbed.
discussion: What might you have missed on a faster walk?
insight: Scale and attention change what we discover. Signs of decomposition can suggest where to look more closely.
resourceLabel: Explore one place over repeat visits

title: One Mushroom, One Record
prompt: Choose one mushroom. Photograph it where it grew, capture a sharp underside view if visible without disturbing it, and note what it was growing on.
group: Compare photos with a partner. Which view or note would help someone who was not there? Take any missing view you can get.
discussion: What would you photograph differently next time?
insight: A useful observation connects visible features, place, and context so someone else can examine the evidence.
